acceptanceCriteria: An explicit writer verb (proposed `pool wait --ticket T --pool P --holder H --ttl-seconds N`, N ≤ policy max) records one WAITING entry in `pools.json` with ticket, priority snapshot, arrival seq and expiry. It is idempotent per request ID, and there is at most one entry per ticket and pool.

A freed member is allocatable only to the head waiter, ordered by (priority, arrival seq), until the waiter claims, the entry expires, or the waiter's ticket stops being eligible. Other claims get `RESOURCE_COLLISION` naming the head.
Expired or ineligible entries never block. `reap` and pool sweep drop them under the existing fencing. A crash between the wait and the claim leaves no stranded member.
`plan preview` and `queue status` show the waitlist (ticket, priority, age, expiresAt) as read-only data.
Opt-in `pools[].handoffGraceSeconds` (default 0) keeps a clean HANDOFF's member reserved for the same ticket's next generation for at most that long. Grace expiry is fenced like a lease.

Filed 2026-10-05 from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#583 (orchestrator triage T583b, read-only code survey on origin/main 019f958a; findings are code-read inferences, not runtime). - Type FEATURE, **P2**: needs owner design decisions (D2, D3), and T583a may be enough. - Labels: `agent-memory`, `ideas`, `github583` - touchPaths: `.corvint/change.cem.json`, `.corvint/changes/`, `docs/TASKS-EXTERNAL-AGENTS.md`, `docs/specs/INDEX.json`, `docs/specs/README.md`, `docs/specs/REQUIREMENTS.tsv`, `docs/specs/corvint-tasks-agent-leases-v0.md`, `internal/tasks/cli/command_help.go`, `internal/tasks/cli/lease.go`, `internal/tasks/cli/plan.go`, `internal/tasks/snapshot/pools.go`, `internal/tasks/transaction/lease_handoff.go`, `internal/tasks/transaction/pools.go`, `internal/tasks/transaction/pool_waitlist_test.go` - Acceptance: 1. An explicit writer verb (proposed `pool wait --ticket T --pool P --holder H --ttl-seconds N`, N ≤ policy max) records one WAITING entry in `pools.json` with ticket, priority snapshot, arrival seq and expiry. It is idempotent per request ID, and there is at most one entry per ticket and pool. 2. A freed member is allocatable only to the head waiter, ordered by (priority, arrival seq), until the waiter claims, the entry expires, or the waiter's ticket stops being eligible. Other claims get `RESOURCE_COLLISION` naming the head. 3. Expired or ineligible entries never block. `reap` and pool sweep drop them under the existing fencing. A crash between the wait and the claim leaves no stranded member. 4. `plan preview` and `queue status` show the waitlist (ticket, priority, age, expiresAt) as read-only data. 5. Opt-in `pools[].handoffGraceSeconds` (default 0) keeps a clean HANDOFF's member reserved for the same ticket's next generation for at most that long. Grace expiry is fenced like a lease. - Depends on: T583a and T584 (both edit `plan.go`).

Owner decisions 2026-10-05 (accepting the orchestrator's recommendations). D2: ship T583a (V1-0784, derived priority yield with no persistent state, batch PR beamfall/corvint#574) first and measure. Build this ticket (T583b) only if starvation persists after V1-0784 lands, for example when a higher-priority ticket is not claimed by anyone. D3, if built: a separate `pool wait` command, so refused claims still commit nothing. Waiters block only lower-priority claims, or same-priority later arrivals, within a time limit of at most 600 s. Handoff grace is opt-in with default 0. Held until V1-0784 starvation evidence exists.
